articles.title: IFA closes with new connections and a thank-you to the team
articles.dek: The foundation’s first IFA booth brought the community together and opened promising conversations for Works with Home Assistant and Sendspin.
body: IFA Berlin is over, and the Open Home Foundation leaves its first appearance as an exhibitor with a lot to be grateful for. The foundation describes the five days as a wonderful experience: a chance to meet the people using and building its projects, spend time together, and make connections that carry beyond the show floor.

A heartfelt thank-you goes to the team that organized the booth, the community meetup and the activities around them. Full-time staff and volunteers made the living-room-style space a welcoming place to stop, sit and talk. The foundation gives special thanks to the volunteers who gave their time and energy to make it happen, and to everyone who came by.

The booth was deliberately not a sales floor: there was nothing to buy and no sales target to meet. That did not make it any less useful for building relationships. The foundation says having a place of its own helped generate many promising leads, alongside the conversations with community members.
The foundation leaves Berlin especially enthusiastic about what those conversations could bring for Works with Home Assistant and Sendspin.

media.alt: People gathered at the Open Home Foundation booth beneath ESPHome, Home Assistant and Music Assistant signs.
media.caption: The team at the Open Home Foundation’s IFA booth. Photo supplied to OHF Daily.

articles.title: Home Assistant puts an Apple device to work on local voice
articles.dek: The app offers speech recognition and spoken replies over the home network, using on-device processing while the app stays open.
body: An Apple device running the Home Assistant app gains another job: processing speech for Home Assistant. A new voice tools server turns audio into text and text into spoken replies using Apple's on-device speech recognition and speech synthesis.

The service is off by default. Enabling it in Settings advertises the device to Home Assistant's Wyoming integration, the connection used for voice services. Processing stays on the Apple device, with transcripts and generated audio returned over the local network.

There is a practical limit: the server answers only while the app is open and stops when it goes into the background. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves contributes the feature, which includes settings for the listening port and lists of the recognition languages and voices available on that device.

articles.title: Home Assistant dashboards gain more ways to choose what appears
articles.dek: Sun, zone, device and template conditions control visibility, with live checks showing whether the rules match.
body: People building Home Assistant dashboards gain more ways to decide when content appears. Visibility rules for dashboards, badges and sections can use sun, zone, device and template conditions, alongside existing checks such as an entity's state or the viewer's screen size.

The editor shows whether individual conditions match and gives an overall visibility result. Rules can combine conditions using all, any or not logic, and content does not flash into view while Home Assistant is still calculating an answer. Existing state and numeric-state rules continue working without requiring a dashboard rewrite.

Petar Petrov contributes the controls and their supporting Home Assistant work. wendevlin reviewed and approved the frontend change; silamon and timmo001 approved the supporting Core change, with review also from Swamp-Ig.
articles.continuity: The supporting change on September 4 lets ordinary user accounts evaluate dashboard conditions; the dashboard editor adds the controls and live visibility feedback.

articles.title: Home Assistant explores automations that act on forecasts
articles.dek: A new proposal would put future prices and sensor readings on their own charts and make them usable without custom templates.
body: Home Assistant is shaping a common way to use predictions from sensors, starting with needs such as finding cheap electricity hours or preparing for a cold night. A proposal opened on September 8 would give integrations a standard way to supply future readings and extend a sensor's chart beyond the present, with the forecast's source clearly identified.

The proposed automation controls include reacting to a newly published forecast, an expected threshold crossing, or the start of the cheapest or most expensive period of a chosen length. Conditions could check whether the forecast stays above a limit or whether the current hour belongs to a set of low-price hours.
The first scope allows one forecast per numeric sensor from its own integration. The architecture and the behavior of triggers when predictions change still need agreement.

externalSources.title: Sensors can show their forecast and automations can act on it

articles.title: Apple Reminders lists connect directly to Home Assistant
articles.dek: The iCloud integration adds editable tasks that sync back to Apple devices, while leaving out reminders it cannot decrypt.
body: Home Assistant's Apple iCloud integration adds editable Apple Reminders lists using the account already configured. Each list becomes a to-do list whose items can be created, renamed, completed or deleted, with descriptions and due dates carried alongside them. Changes sync back to the user's Apple devices.

Subtasks appear as ordinary items placed beneath their parents, without a nested relationship. Reminders that the integration cannot decrypt under Apple's Advanced Data Protection are omitted, preventing an edit from replacing their real text with unreadable placeholders. Previously deleted lists can still appear as empty lists.
Federico Zivolo contributes the feature, with review and approval from joostlek.
articles.continuity: The August 31 edition covered read-only iCloud calendars; this adds editable reminders using the same configured account.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows which integrations share a Modbus connection
articles.dek: A new Connectivity panel brings shared wired connections into one view and links them to the integrations using them.
body: People connecting energy meters, solar inverters or heating equipment through Modbus gain a clearer view of their shared connections in Home Assistant. A new panel in Connectivity lists each physical endpoint once and shows the integrations using it, making a shared serial bus or gateway visible in one place.

The panel builds on Home Assistant's shared Modbus connection service and a new connection inventory. Its open-or-closed indicator describes the current link state: devices can close an idle connection and reopen it when an integration next polls. Serial ports carrying Modbus traffic also link through to the panel.

The work advances the Open Home Foundation's approved roadmap opportunity for a Modbus entry point in Settings. The planned scope is viewing connections and navigating between them; adding, editing and removing connections remain outside this first iteration.

articles.title: Home Assistant explores a way back after an automation goes wrong
articles.dek: A rewritten proposal focuses on readable version history and restoring an earlier automation while keeping later changes recoverable.
body: Home Assistant is shaping a way to recover a working automation after a saved edit breaks it. The proposal would let people inspect earlier versions and restore one from the automation editor, without rolling back a whole installation to recover a single automation. In a September 9 comment, Niels says he has rewritten the opportunity and moved it into Shaping.

The proposed history would show when each version was saved, who or what changed it—including an AI assistant—and a readable explanation of the differences. Restoring an older version would create another history entry, keeping the version it replaced recoverable. The initial scope covers automations held in Home Assistant's storage; automations defined in YAML files are excluded.

The design still needs decisions on how long to keep versions, how to explain changes without requiring people to read configuration code, and what happens when a restored automation refers to a device that no longer exists.

externalSources.title: Give users a way back to a working configuration

articles.title: Music Assistant stops two routes to the wrong track
articles.dek: Direct audio links from Home Assistant and selections deep in Plex queues keep the listener's choice intact.
body: Music Assistant fixes two cases where asking for one piece of audio could start another. Home Assistant playback requests for a direct link no longer fall through to a name search when the user has a filter limiting their music providers. Plex Connect also keeps the selected track when it sits beyond the first 100 queue entries.

Direct links and local files bypass the provider filter during verification. For Plex, the 100-item queue limit starts at the chosen track, with earlier entries filling any remaining space for repeat playback. Very large queues can still have incomplete wrap-around coverage when the fetched portion does not reach the beginning. Marvin Schenkel contributes both fixes.

articles.title: Home Assistant approves a clearer way to choose automation triggers
articles.dek: The proposed editor would identify what started an automation without asking users to invent and remember trigger names.
body: Home Assistant has approved a plan to make it easier to choose which event should lead to which action in an automation. Instead of asking people to assign an identifier and recognize it later, the editor would show the trigger itself in the condition picker and create a stable identifier in the background. Franck Nijhof recorded the approval on September 8 after a discussion at IFA.

The proposal keeps existing manually assigned identifiers compatible, with future manual editing handled through YAML. It would also clean up references when an automatically identified trigger is removed through the interface, and flag missing or duplicate references.

externalSources.title: Improve referencing triggers in automation conditions and actions

articles.title: The foundation plans an iOS app handover that preserves home setups
articles.dek: A transition proposal aims to preserve registrations and notification automations if an App Store transfer cannot be arranged.
body: The Open Home Foundation is planning how to move ownership of Home Assistant's iOS app while limiting disruption to people who already use it. A September 8 update introduces a migration proposal covering existing installations, fresh installs, notification automations, managed devices and beta users.

The roadmap pursues another attempt to transfer the existing App Store listing and develops a fallback if that fails. Under the proposed fallback, a successor app would take over the existing Home Assistant registration, with the aim of preserving device and entity identities and notification targets. The old app would guide people through the handover.

The plan also needs to account for people who never reopen the old app. The public roadmap identifies interrupted notifications and confusion between two App Store listings as risks the handover must address.

externalSources.title: Move companion app ownership to the foundation

articles.title: Home Assistant shapes clearer warnings for uncertified Matter devices
articles.dek: The revised plan focuses on explaining recoverable certification problems and letting the person adding a device decide.
body: Home Assistant is shaping a more specific response when a Matter device cannot prove its certification during setup. A September 8 update separates that decision from the work on how devices connect, giving the warning and confirmation experience its own scope.

The proposal would explain which vendor or product information could not be verified and offer a per-device choice for recoverable cases, such as test credentials. A revoked certificate would continue to prevent setup. Devices added without verified certification would retain a visible indication afterward.

externalSources.title: Let users decide how to handle uncertified Matter devices during commissioning

articles.title: ESPHome keeps Sonoff radio captures running past the first signal
articles.dek: Two fixes restore continuous, complete recordings from 433 MHz remotes on bridges running Portisch firmware.
body: Makers capturing signals from 433 MHz remotes with a Sonoff RF Bridge could receive one recording and then nothing more. ESPHome corrects the response that inadvertently switched Portisch firmware out of its raw capture mode after the first signal—even if that signal was background radio activity. It also stops valid recordings being cut short when their data contains a byte mistaken for an end marker.

Bryan Li reports verifying the fixes on a Sonoff RF Bridge R2 and running the same logic across seven bridges. This is his first contribution to ESPHome, with review and approval from jesserockz. The correction requires no configuration change.

pullRequests.title: [rf_bridge] Fix bucket sniffing with Portisch firmware

articles.title: ESPHome keeps Anova cookers on the chosen temperature scale
articles.dek: A Bluetooth correction restores Fahrenheit when a cooker drifts back to Celsius and prevents misconverted readings.
body: An Anova Precision Cooker connected through ESPHome can revert from Fahrenheit to Celsius without being asked, leaving its display and converted readings out of step. ESPHome reapplies the configured temperature scale before each status check instead of setting it only when Bluetooth first connects.

Contributor raykholo tested the correction on a Bluetooth-only Precision Cooker 1.0: the display returned to Fahrenheit without restarting the ESP32, and temperatures tracked correctly while heating from Home Assistant. This is raykholo's first contribution to ESPHome, with review and approval from jesserockz.
